$comment: Gemfall beat 7, the Reckoning's chapter 7 (docs/campaigns/gemfall.md, 7R). Every ending sets climbed_the_mountain. The seal clock is set exactly once per path: scene_caravan_won (clock_steady), scene_caravan_lost (clock_late), or ending_scattered (clock_late, the lost-fight setback). Faction plays read the allies set; road callbacks read road, crossing, ember and sprites. facet_caravan is defined in gemfall-07h. Pacing episodes on the spine (Odo's barrow, the noon shake, Posy's stone, the haul vote, the last moth, the morning slide, the lookout, the downhill crowd, the last-climb vote) set only chapter-local flags.
title: The Returning

objectives.label: Turned the Caravan Stone around for home
Talked Hessa out of her mask
Sent the wolf pack down an easier road

ossley_debt_stone.name: Ossley's Wet Stone
ossley_debt_stone.text: A plain river stone, always a little wet. Carry it up, and thank the river.

scene_the_pinch.narration: Every road in the realm squeezes through one gap between two red hills. The dragonlings call it the Pinch. Wagons, carts, and one man pushing a wheelbarrow full of glitter all shove through it at once. The ground gives a small shrug, like a sleeping dog, and you notice the embermoths that always live here are simply gone.

choices.label: Count the shakes the way the grandmothers taught you

scene_the_pinch_count_shakes.narration: Your dragonling counts the shakes the way the grandmothers taught: a slow breath between each. Four breaths. Then four. Then three and a half. "Grandmother says three is when you ring," your dragonling says, and does not say what comes after three.

scene_glitter_barrow.narration: Right in the middle of the Pinch, the man with the wheelbarrow full of glitter is stuck. His name is Odo, his wheel is jammed between two rocks, and forty wagons behind him are shouting. "It's all gems," Odo tells you proudly. Most of it is painted gravel. But somewhere in that barrow, one thing is humming.

check_glitter_barrow.prompt: Heave Odo's wheelbarrow out of the Pinch

onSuccess.narration: With a grunt and a heave, the barrow pops free and forty wagons cheer. Odo is so grateful he digs through the glitter and hands you the humming thing: a real stone, warm as a teapot. "Keeps me up at night," he says. "Singing."

onFailure.narration: You heave. The wheel pops off entirely and rolls away down the hill, and half the Pinch runs after it. In all the fuss the barrow tips, and one real stone rolls out humming at your feet. Odo waves at you to keep it. He is busy chasing a wheel.

scene_glitter_barrow_sort.narration: You tip the glitter onto a blanket and sort it, bit by bit. Painted gravel. Painted gravel. A button. Painted gravel. And one real stone, warm and humming. Odo stares at his barrow of gravel for a long time. Then he shrugs, hands you the stone, and says, "Well. Gravel doesn't sing at night, I suppose."

scene_glitter_barrow_under.narration: Your bigfoot crouches and looks where nobody else thought to. The wheel is not jammed. It is sitting on a glassback crab, who has decided Odo's barrow is a gem deposit and is guarding it very seriously. One polite tap on the shell and the crab scuttles off, offended. Odo is so grateful he hands you the one real stone in his barrow.

choice_how.narration: Stones are pouring north, and you want them pouring home. That is a lot of stones to turn around. Who is helping?

choices.label: Work quietly, the way only you know how
Do it on your own, with a handcart and a sign

scene_wardens.narration: The wardens did exactly what you told them would work. Overnight their checkpoint grew a gate, a ledger and a very long table, and every stone goes into a numbered box. It works. A small faun watches her one shiny pebble get a number, and her lip wobbles.

choices.label: Ask for the pebble back. It is only a pebble.

scene_wardens_let_work.narration: You let the wardens work. It is quick and it is fair and nobody enjoys it, least of all the wardens. Box after numbered box fills with humming stones, and the sergeant writes every number down twice, and the small faun's pebble gets a number too. It works. You keep telling yourself it works.

scene_wardens_pebble.narration: "It's only a pebble," you say. The sergeant looks at the pebble, looks at the box, looks at the ledger, and then does something that is not in any ledger: hands it back. The small faun holds it in both hands and gives you a honeycake she had been saving for a very bad day, which this now is not.

scene_grandmothers.narration: The dragonling towns have turned gathering law inside out. A grandmother sits outside every gem-buyer's tent, knitting, saying "No, dear," until the buyer feels so bad he hands his stones over himself. One buyer is crying into a very expensive hat.

choices.label: Keep the queue of sorry buyers moving

scene_grandmothers_queue.narration: You keep the queue of sorry buyers moving. It is a long queue and they are very sorry. One of them tries to leave without handing anything over, and three grandmothers say "No, dear" at once, in harmony, and he comes back without a word and empties both pockets.

scene_grandmothers_knit.narration: A grandmother hands you needles and wool without looking up. You do not know how to knit. By the end of the morning you know how to knit badly, and two gem-buyers have handed over their sacks rather than watch you drop another stitch. "That's the trick," says the grandmother. "Nobody can stand it."

check_handcart.prompt: Talk travelers into letting their stones go home

onSuccess.narration: A handcart, a sign that says STONES GOING HOME, and a lot of honest talking. By lunchtime the cart is half full, and somebody has drawn a smiley face on the sign.

onFailure.narration: Most people walk straight past the sign. One man gives you a stone, asks for it back, then gives it again. The cart is nearly empty, but at least you know which wagons hum the loudest.

scene_noon_shake.narration: At noon the ground gives a big shrug, bigger than the morning ones. Every sack on the road jumps. One splits open, and its stones spill out and start to roll. Not downhill. Uphill. Slowly, all together, toward the mountain, like ducklings following their mother. A warden drops his pencil.

choices.label: Catch them before they roll away
Follow them and see where they stop

variants.text: Your own packs hum, but none of the runaways are yours. They are all strangers' stones, and they seem to know the way better than you do.
The great stones in your packs tug at their straps, wanting to follow. You hold on tight.
Your packs go wild. The great stones in them rattle and strain at the straps, and you have to sit on one pack to keep it from rolling off after the rest.

check_noon_shake.prompt: Scoop up a sack of stones that are rolling the wrong way

onSuccess.narration: You dive, scoop and juggle. Every last stone ends up in your arms, still humming, still leaning gently uphill, like puppies pulling on a lead.

onFailure.narration: The stones slip through your fingers and roll straight into a goat pen. The goat gives them back one at a time, very slowly, and wants a scratch behind the ears for every single one.

scene_noon_shake_follow.narration: You follow them up the road. They roll as far as the last red rock before the slope, then stop in a neat line, all pointing the same way: straight at Mount Red Sky. You pick them up gently. They feel, somehow, a little disappointed.

choices.label: Carry them back to the pile

scene_noon_shake_harvest.narration: You hold up the Harvest Stone, and the rolling stones change their minds. One by one they turn and roll to your feet instead, and sit there humming along with it, like a choir that has found its note. The warden picks up his pencil and writes that down.

scene_road_gifts.narration: By afternoon something strange starts happening. The road begins bringing things back to you: things you did on the way here, walking up the hill on their own legs, as if the whole realm had been keeping your receipts.

choices.label: A flat boat is coming up the dry creek
A MossHome runner is waving a knotted cord
A boggart is sidling up with a satchel
A boggart is sidling up with a satchel
Someone in a pointed hat is pushing to the front

scene_ossley.narration: A frog in a very old hat is poling a flat boat up a creek with no water in it. Nobody asks how. It is the frog from the reeds of the Great River, and the name painted on the side of his boat is OLD OSSLEY. The boat is full of stones: every one the river took off somebody this season, and a lot of "misplaced" ones. "Stones want to go home," he says. "We only kept them until someone was going that way."

choices.label: Ask what you still owe him from the river
Load his stones onto your cart

scene_ossley_debt.narration: Ossley takes a long time to answer, which is how Ossley answers. His price is not coin. It never was. He presses one plain, wet stone into your hand: "Carry this one up with your own hands. When you put it down, say thank you to the river."

scene_mosshome_runner.narration: A MossHome runner jogs up with moss in her hair and a string of grumbling mules behind her. She counts the knots on your cord twice, nods, and unloads everything the Woods confiscated from careless hunters: shovels, a teapot, one very surprised hat, and stones. Lots of stones.

scene_boggart.narration: A boggart with a satchel full of scribbled paper sidles up beside you, not looking at you, and says to nobody: "Catalog. Who bought what in the marsh. Very interesting. Costs one really good sentence you overheard."

choices.label: Tell it what Dunmore shouted on the grandmother's doorstep
Tell it what Grandmother Tull said about the unused bell

scene_boggart_grandma_said.narration: You tell it what Grandmother Tull said about the bell nobody rings, word for word, including the second time she said it. The boggart closes its eyes to listen and keeps them closed for some time afterwards. "Lovely," it says to nobody. "Lovely." The catalog is in your hands before you notice it has let go.

scene_boggart_wardens_said.narration: "It hums!" you shout, in Dunmore's exact voice, pointing at nothing at all. The boggart shivers all over with delight and writes it down twice, once forwards and once backwards. "Oh, that's a good one. That's a keeper." It hands over the catalog without ever once looking at you.

scene_ford_witch.narration: It is Mother Thrum, the witch from the ford queue, in her pointed hat, with a wool sock tucked under one arm. Something in the sock is ringing. She has walked the whole road north for this. "I always ask twice," she says. "Once at the ford, and once at the mountain. What do you actually want?"

choices.label: "Honestly? We are still working it out."

scene_ford_witch_not_sure.narration: "Honestly? We're still working it out." Mother Thrum nods slowly, as if that is a better answer than most. She keeps her ringing sock. She gives you a songbird ribbon instead, "for the working out," and says she will ask again, because she always does.

scene_ford_witch_put_back.narration: "To put them all back," you say. Mother Thrum looks at you for a long moment over her spectacles. Then she unwraps the sock and sets a stone from the ford in your hands, and for the first time since the ford it stops ringing. "There," she says. "That was the answer. Took you long enough."

scene_posy.narration: Coming up the road is a tired prospector called Corbin, with his daughter Posy on his shoulders. They spent everything they had to get here. Posy is holding one small stone in both fists, and it hums whenever she squeezes it. "It's my lucky one," she tells you. "It's going to make us rich." Corbin looks at your stones going home and says nothing.

choices.label: Tell Posy where her stone wants to go
Let her keep it, and wish them luck
Show her the sprites' tiny medal

check_posy.prompt: Help a little girl decide to give up her lucky stone

onSuccess.narration: You tell Posy about the mountain and the hum, the gentle version. She thinks about it very hard. Then she opens her fists and puts the stone on your pile herself. "So it can go home," she says. Corbin lets out a breath he has been holding since spring.

onFailure.narration: Posy listens, and then hides the stone behind her back. "It's mine," she says, and her lip wobbles. You do not push. Corbin gives you a small, sorry nod, and the two of them go on up the road toward the camps.

scene_posy_let_keep.narration: You wish them luck, and mean it. Posy waves the stone at you over her father's head as they go, and you can hear it humming all the way round the corner. You hope the mountain will not mind one small stone for a little while longer.

scene_posy_medal.narration: You show Posy the sprites' woven medal, the tiny one that says NOT. She has never seen anything so small or so important. "You got a medal for not taking something?" She looks at her stone. She looks at the medal. Then she puts the stone on your pile, and asks very seriously whether sprites give medals to girls.

scene_masks.narration: Further down the road, people in painted bark masks are running the same funnel backwards, collecting stones gently from anyone who will hand them over. "We'll break it properly, all at once, so it can be fixed properly," one of them says. You know that voice. It is Hessa from the soup tent, with her ladle still on her belt.

choices.label: Borrow a mask and walk right into their camp
Let them be, and keep working your side of the road

scene_masks_let_be.narration: You let them be, and work your own side of the road. For a while you and the masks pass stones in opposite directions ten paces apart, like a very slow dance, and once Hessa looks up and nods to you, and you nod back, and neither of you stops.

scene_masks_mask_swap.narration: Your kitsune borrows a mask from a hook on a cart, pulls it down, and walks straight into the masks' camp humming along with everybody else. Twenty minutes later your kitsune walks out again with a sack of stones "for the break" and a bowl of soup, and nobody is any the wiser. The soup is very good.

check_tamsin.prompt: Convince Hessa the seal is not a cage

onSuccess.narration: Hessa takes off her mask. "I only wanted somebody to fix things," she says quietly. She hands you her whole sack of stones, and then her ladle, and asks you to fix things.

onFailure.narration: She listens kindly, all the way to the end. Then she puts her mask back on. "I hope you're right," she says. "I don't think you are." Her cell rolls on with a full sack.

choice_haul.narration: The afternoon is going, and your pile of going-home stones has grown far too big to carry. It has to get up the hill to the dragonling way-shelter before dark, where it will be safe. The ground shrugs again, as if to say hurry. How are you going to move it?

choices.label: Borrow a snowhorn goat from the dragonlings
Everybody carry a sackful up the hill
Build a sledge out of a broken door
Carry strangers' stones up the hill, one trip at a time

variants.text: None of the pile is yours, only what strangers have trusted you with.
A few great stones of your own ride on top of the pile, humming louder the nearer the hill gets.
Your own great stones are the loudest in the pile, and they tug uphill like a team of eager dogs.

check_haul_goat.prompt: Make friends with a grumpy snowhorn goat

onSuccess.narration: The goat sniffs you, sniffs the cart, and decides you are acceptable. It pulls the whole load up the hill at a steady trot, stopping only once, to eat the corner of your sign.

onFailure.narration: The goat sits down. It will not move. In the end you pull the cart on your own, and the goat rides on top of the stones, looking very pleased with itself, all the way to the shelter.

check_haul_carry.prompt: Carry the whole pile up the hill, sack by sack

onSuccess.narration: You make a chain up the hill and pass the sacks along, hand to hand, singing a counting song. Strangers on the road join in. By the top the chain is forty people long, and nobody remembers who started it.

onFailure.narration: Halfway up, your arms turn to noodles. You sit down on the sacks to rest, and a passing grandmother tuts, hitches your cart to her own wagon, and tows the lot up the hill without a word.

check_haul_sledge.prompt: Build a sledge that slides uphill

onSuccess.narration: Rope, a broken door and some greased planks. The sledge glides up the slope on its runners like a dream, and a crowd of dragonling children follow it all the way to the shelter, asking for a turn.

onFailure.narration: The sledge works beautifully, in the wrong direction. It slides gently back to the bottom of the hill twice before you think to tie it to a tree and winch it up, one heave at a time. It gets there. Eventually.

choice_haul_others.narration: Your own arms are empty, so you fill them with everybody else's. Travelers press sacks into your arms and tell you which camp they came from. You climb, set a sack down in the way-shelter's yard, and climb down for another. Nobody keeps count of the trips. By dusk the yard is full, and the stones hum like they know who carried them.

scene_evening.narration: Evening on the Pinch. The going-home stones are stacked safe in the way-shelter's yard, humming. Below you, campfires pop up all along the road like a string of beads, and the ground keeps shrugging, a little more often than this morning.

choices.label: Listen to the singers at the campfires
An Exchange caravan rolls in, and someone is waving
Sit down at a campfire full of strangers
Go up to the way-shelter to sleep

variants.text: None of the stones in the yard are yours, but they hum just as loudly, and nobody asks whose they were.
A few great stones from your own packs sit among them, humming along.
The great stones from your own packs hum loudest, a whole choir in one heap.

scene_evening_campfire.narration: You sit down at a campfire with a family of fauns, a warden off duty, and a prospector with one boot. Everybody is talking about the shaking. The prospector says it is nothing. The warden says nothing at all, which is worse. Then the faun children ask how you got here, and make you tell the funny bit twice.

choices.label: Go up to the way-shelter to sleep

scene_relay_sing.narration: The relay singers have new verses, and the verses are about wagons that have not arrived yet. You can hear tomorrow's traffic tonight. Then a grandmother's runner hands you a list of caves nobody may ever dig, and it is exactly where you would put a seal.

choices.label: Fold the list away and get some sleep

scene_ember.narration: "Darlings! From the docks!" Madame Coralie Fenn is lashed to the top of the caravan in her barrel on wheels, waving with both arms. She remembers you fondly. She also remembers the warm red stone you sold her on the quay, your very first one. It is right here in a velvet box with a new gold label, FIRST STONE OF THE REALM, and its price has gone up a very great deal since then.

choices.label: Buy it back, whatever it costs
Wave, and let it go on its way

scene_ember_wave.narration: You wave. Madame Fenn waves back with both arms and the barrel wobbles alarmingly on its lashings. "Next time, darlings!" she calls, and the caravan rolls on toward the camps with your very first stone humming in a velvet box on top of it. You watch until the lanterns turn the corner.

scene_ember_buy_back.narration: You pay what Madame Fenn asks, which is a great deal, and she counts it twice and hugs the velvet box before she hands it over. "I always hoped it would be you, darlings," she says, and seems to mean it. The stone is warm as toast, exactly as you remember, and it hums as if it remembers you too.

scene_last_moth.narration: At the way-shelter door, something small bumps against the lantern. Tap. Tap. It is an embermoth, glowing like a coal, the first one you have seen all day. Every other moth flew south days ago. This one is going the wrong way, and it looks very tired.

choices.label: Let it into the lantern to rest
Cup it in your hands and send it south

scene_last_moth_lantern.narration: You open the little lantern door, and the moth crawls in and settles beside the wick as if it had been looking for exactly that. It glows a bit brighter. The shelter cat watches it all night and does not blink once.

scene_last_moth_south.narration: You cup it in your hands, carry it to the south wall, and open them. The moth sits warm on your palm for a moment. Then it lifts off and drifts away down the valley after the others, a tiny spark getting smaller. It is the right way. It still feels lonely to watch.

scene_last_moth_feel.narration: Your unicorn touches the moth with the very tip of the horn and goes quiet. "It isn't lost," your unicorn says. "It's homesick. It wants to go up, not down. It just can't go alone." The moth climbs into your unicorn's mane and stays there all night, glowing.

rest_way_shelter.narration: The dragonling way-shelter has its bell tied up with ribbon so nobody rings it by accident. There is soup, and a cat, and a whole wall of children's drawings of the mountain. Patch up your scrapes. Tomorrow is the worst bend.

choices.label: Up the switchback at first light

scene_morning_slide.narration: In the night the mountain shrugged so hard that half a hillside slid onto the road. A heap of red rocks taller than a wagon sits right across it. A warden stands in front of it with a clipboard, writing ROAD CLOSED in very small letters, as if that will help.

choices.label: Follow where Ossley's reed knot drips

check_morning_slide.prompt: Find the one rock that holds up all the others, and pull

onSuccess.narration: You find the one rock that holds up all the rest, and pull. The whole heap shrugs, sighs, and slides politely off the edge of the road. The warden crosses out CLOSED and writes OPEN, in slightly bigger letters.

onFailure.narration: The big rock will not budge. But behind it, between two boulders, there is a gap just wide enough to wriggle through. You come out the other side red with dust from head to toe, and the warden writes that down too.

scene_morning_slide_goat_path.narration: There is a goat path above the slide, about as wide as a sandwich. You go round in single file, one careful step at a time, not looking down. A snowhorn goat coming the other way stops, considers you, and steps politely aside onto what appears to be nothing at all.

scene_morning_slide_verses.narration: You sing the Spiral Verses from the rush road, in order, the way the relay taught. One verse is about this very hill: an old cart track that curls round the back of it. And there it is, behind the gorse. The warden watches you go and decides not to write anything down at all.

scene_morning_slide_reed_knot.narration: Ossley's reed knot, which never dries, starts dripping sideways. You follow the drips to a dry stream bed that runs right under the slide through a tunnel of old roots, and out the other side. Ossley would say nothing about this. You say nothing either. It seems polite.

scene_switchback.narration: The road zigzags up to the worst bend, and coming down it, the wrong way, is a pack of cinder wolves. They are not hunting. They are leaving the mountain, and you are standing in their way.

choices.label: Give them an easier way down
Follow the trail of tiny tied grass knots
Fly ahead and find a side path

scene_switchback_fly_round.narration: You go up, find a side path the wolves have not thought of, and lead everyone along it one careful step at a time. The pack streams down the main road beneath you in a long gray ribbon, and one wolf glances up, and decides you are not worth the climb.

scene_switchback_sprite_knots.narration: Somebody has been here before you. Tiny knots of grass, tied at ankle height, lead off the road and along a goat path above the zigzags. Harvest sprites, this far north, still looking out for you. You follow the knots, and the wolves pour past below you without ever looking up.

check_wolves.prompt: Roll a smoked sausage down the side trail at exactly the right moment

onSuccess.narration: The sausage bounces down the side trail, and the whole pack follows it with enormous dignity, as if that was where they were going all along.

onFailure.narration: The sausage bounces off a rock and lands right back at your feet. The wolves look at the sausage. Then they look at you.

encounter_wolves.narration: The pack spreads out across the zigzags, ears flat, too frightened of the mountain to think straight.

onVictory.narration: The pack decides you are more trouble than the road is worth, and pours past you down the hill in a long gray ribbon.

onDefeat.narration: The wolves bowl straight through you and keep going. Nobody is hurt, but the cart is on its side and the stones are rolling every which way down the hill.

scene_bend_lookout.narration: You reach the worst bend with an hour to spare. Far below, a long caravan is winding up the zigzags, twelve wagons long and slow as honey. There is time to get ready. Not much. The ground hums under your boots now, steady, like someone humming a song they cannot remember the end of.

choices.label: Creep down and look the caravan over
Paint a big sign for the caravan to read
Hold up the Table Stone and listen

check_bend_scout.prompt: Sneak along the ridge and pick out the humming wagon

onSuccess.narration: You creep along the ridge and watch. Mules with cotton in their ears. A caravan master rubbing her head every few minutes, as if it aches. And the middle wagon, humming so hard its canvas trembles. You know exactly where to go now.

onFailure.narration: You creep along the ridge, slip on loose gravel, and slide most of the way down to the road on your bottom. A mule looks at you. You look at the mule. Neither of you tells anybody, and you scramble back up just in time.

scene_bend_lookout_sign.narration: You paint STONES GOING HOME in letters as tall as a goat on an old tent, and stretch it between two rocks at the bend. It is a bit wonky. One S is backwards. It is, without any question, the biggest sign on the mountain.

scene_bend_lookout_table_stone.narration: You hold up the Table Stone, and from far below, the middle wagon answers it. Two stones humming to each other across a valley, like two cows calling over a field. Now you know exactly which wagon it is, and roughly how loud it will be when it gets here. Very.

choice_the_bend.narration: The north road's worst bend: a hairpin over a long drop, where every wagon has to slow right down. Here comes the fattest caravan in the funnel, twelve wagons long. In the middle wagon something hums so loudly the mules have cotton in their ears.

choices.label: You heard this caravan in last night's song. Be waiting.
Swap the stone while nobody is looking
You know from the catalog who it was sold to
Show the caravan master your cart full of stones going home
Recite the one rule to the caravan master
Walk straight up to the humming wagon you picked out

choice_the_bend_heard_it.narration: You heard this caravan in last night's verse, and you are at the bend an hour before it is. When the lead wagon comes round the hairpin, you are already sitting on the rock it has to stop at, and the caravan master looks at you as if you have cheated, which, in a way, you have.

choices.label: Go and meet the caravan master

choice_the_bend_relay.narration: You cup your hands and give a sharp whistle toward the relay road. A centaur appears on the ridge almost before the sound has faded, with two more behind her. Between them they turn the fattest caravan in the funnel off the main road and to a stop right in front of you, as neatly as threading a needle.

choices.label: Go and meet the caravan master

check_caravan_helped.prompt: Ask the caravan master to send the humming stone home, with help at your back

onSuccess.narration: The caravan master looks at you, at the help behind you, at the shaking ground, and sighs a sigh that goes all the way down to her boots. "Fine. Take it. It's been giving me headaches."

onFailure.narration: She almost says yes. Then the ground lurches, the mules bolt, and in the muddle a masked wagoneer steers the middle wagon off up a side track.

check_caravan.prompt: Convince a tired caravan master to give up the best stone she has ever carried

onSuccess.narration: You tell her the whole truth, from the humming to the seal. She is quiet for a long time. Then she climbs into the middle wagon and comes back holding the stone in both hands.

onFailure.narration: She has heard a lot of stories this season. She does not believe yours. While you are still arguing, a masked wagoneer quietly steers the middle wagon off up a side track.

scene_caravan_won.narration: The Caravan Stone is the size of a loaf of bread and hums like a whole choir. The moment it is pointed back up the mountain, the humming changes key, and sounds, very faintly, relieved. The next tremor is a little softer than the last.

choices.label: Carry it on up the mountain

scene_caravan_lost.narration: The masks have the humming stone. A cell of masks drives it away up the side track, and one of them waves to you, apologetically. Behind them the ground stops shrugging and starts shaking, slow and steady, like a drum.

choices.label: Climb anyway, with what you have

scene_downhill_crowd.narration: Higher up, the whole road is coming the other way. Wagons, wardens, a family of fauns with all their chairs tied to a mule. Everyone is going down. Right beside you, the fauns' little cart drops a wheel into a crack in the road and sticks fast, and the smallest faun starts to cry.

choices.label: Put your shoulders to the cart
Carry their things across the crack
Someone small is running up the hill toward you
Wave down Odo and his wheelbarrow

check_downhill_cart.prompt: Heave a faun cart out of a crack in the road

onSuccess.narration: One, two, three, heave! The wheel pops out of the crack and the cart rolls on. The fauns shout thank you all the way down the hill, and the smallest one throws you a very squashed flower.

onFailure.narration: Heave as you might, the wheel stays stuck. So you lift the whole cart out instead, which takes everybody, the mule and a passing warden. The fauns say thank you seven times each.

scene_downhill_crowd_unload.narration: You carry everything across the crack: six chairs, a cooking pot, a birdcage with no bird in it, and the smallest faun, who stops crying to ride on your shoulders. Empty, the cart lifts out easily. You load it all again on the far side, and wave them off down the hill.

scene_downhill_crowd_posy.narration: It is Posy, running up while everyone else runs down, with Corbin puffing behind her. She pushes her lucky stone into your hand. "It kept humming at night," she says. "I think it was asking. You take it home." Then Corbin gets his shoulder under the faun cart and pops it free, and they all go down together.

scene_downhill_crowd_odo.narration: Odo comes clattering down the hill with his empty wheelbarrow, which turns out to be exactly the right size for six chairs and a small faun. Everyone piles in. Odo wheels the lot round the crack, singing. "Never carried anything worth this much," he says, and he means the fauns.

choice_last_climb.narration: Above the last houses the road splits in two. To the left, a warden stair cut straight up the rock, steep and quick. To the right, the old dragonling path, which wanders and doubles back and takes its time. Behind you, the ground shakes in a slow, steady beat, like a drum. Which way up?

check_last_climb_stair.prompt: Race up a steep stair before the light goes

onSuccess.narration: Up and up and up, two steps at a time. You reach the top with your legs wobbling and your heart thumping, well ahead of the dark.

onFailure.narration: Halfway up, a tremor shakes loose a shower of little stones. You press flat against the rock and wait, and then climb on carefully, one step at a time, and reach the top dusty but whole, just as the light turns orange.

choice_last_climb_old_path.narration: The old path wanders, but it is kind. It finds the shade, the flat bits, a spring of cold water, and a carved stone at every bend with a little dragonling face on it, smiling. You count eleven faces. By the twelfth you are at the tree line, and nobody's legs hurt at all.

choice_last_climb_moth.narration: The little embermoth lifts off and flies ahead of you, up neither path, along a ledge nobody else had noticed. It glows at every turn so you can find it. At the tree line it circles above you once, like a thank you, and flies on up the mountain, toward home.

rest_tree_line.narration: At the tree line you stop and look back. Everyone else on the road is running downhill: wagons, wardens, masks, a man with an empty wheelbarrow. There is not a single embermoth left in the foothills. You turn around and walk up the mountain everyone else is running away from, with your arms full of stones that want to go home.

variants.text: At the tree line you stop and look back. Everyone else on the road is running downhill: wagons, wardens, masks, a man with an empty wheelbarrow. There is not a single embermoth left in the foothills. You turn around and walk up the mountain everyone else is running away from, with your hands empty and your packs humming, to see what you can still do.
Every great stone you carry hums all the way up, one voice after another, like a choir climbing a stair.

ending_scattered.narration: By the time you have found half the stones, the fattest caravan has gone past the bend without you. The ground is shaking in a slow, patient rhythm now, like a heartbeat. Everyone else is running down the mountain. You pick up what you can carry and go up it anyway, a long way behind.

scene_quiet_work.narration: You tell nobody what you are for. You just start. A stone slipped out of a sack here, a pocket emptied into a better pocket there, a wagon that reaches the camps one crate lighter than it left. Nobody notices, which is the point, and by noon the pile behind your tent is humming.

voiceGuide.tone: warm, urgent, a little spooky but never scary; the realm sending back what the party gave it

npcVoices.hessa: Deep Hollow cell member who ran the soup tent; gentle, sad, sure she is helping; says 'properly' a lot
npcVoices.old_ossley: very few words, long pauses that are not hesitation, answers the question you meant
npcVoices.warden_sergeant: rigid, honest, tired; counts everything; secretly hates making children cry
npcVoices.grandmother: dragonling gatherer; knits while she talks; 'No, dear' is a complete sentence
npcVoices.mosshome_runner: breathless, cheerful, counts knots out loud
npcVoices.boggart: talks sidelong to nobody, never meets your eye, treasures overheard sentences
npcVoices.ford_witch: Mother Thrum, the ford witch; pointed hat, dry, kind underneath; only asks one question and means it
npcVoices.exchange_merchant: Madame Coralie Fenn, the Exchange gem-buyer in a barrel on wheels; delighted to see you, genuinely fond, calls everyone darlings, and still a merchant
npcVoices.caravan_master: exhausted, practical, has had a headache since the stone came aboard
npcVoices.odo: a cheerful man with a wheelbarrow of painted gravel he believes is gems; proud, easily delighted, never sulks
npcVoices.posy: Corbin the prospector's small daughter; serious, brave, thinks hard before she answers
